lines.t: [Intro — distant static, low pulse]
[Overlapping fictional news voices]
“Unexplained atmospheric disturbances…”
“Reports of disappearances across multiple regions…”
“Seismic activity is increasing—”
[All sound cuts]
Then the ground began to speak.
A ring of light above the ocean,
A stopped car running in the rain.
A mother calling through a doorway,
But no one answers to their name.
Empty shoes beside a bedside,
An open book upon a chair.
Across the world, the same bewilderment:
Someone loved is no more there.
Before the sirens find their rhythm,
Before the breaking story ends,
The pavement rises like a wave—
The towers buckle, bridges bend.
Missing faces.
Shaking foundations.
Every screen becomes a flame.
And beneath a thousand voices,
Something waits to give it a name.
The first harvest—
His children gathered home.
And the earth cries out beneath
The weight of what the world is shown.
Glory to the Lord of heaven!
Glory to the righteous King!
The great and terrible Day is declared—
Let every nation hear His witnesses sing.
Then come the voices, calm and polished:
“Do not believe the ancient words.
Visitors have crossed the darkness;
This is contact with other worlds.”
They show us scales beneath a spotlight,
Reptilian faces on a screen.
They call the missing “relocated,”
And claim to know what no one’s seen.
“Your families live beyond the heavens.
Your rescue waits beyond the blue.”
But borrowed wonders dress the falsehood;
A dazzling sign can lie to you.
Not every traveler is the enemy.
Not every stranger serves the night.
But here the dragon sells his story,
And calls surrender “seeing light.”
The first harvest—
His children gathered home.
And the earth cries out beneath
The weight of what the world is shown.
Glory to the Lord of heaven!
Glory to the righteous King!
The great and terrible Day is declared—
Let every nation hear His witnesses sing.
[Instrumental — earthquake impacts, brass, then silence]
Through broken streets and falling ashes,
Through cameras raised and armies drawn,
His witnesses stand unpurchased,
And speak though all the world looks on.
They give the glory to no creature,
No vessel burning through the sky.
They name YahuShua as salvation;
They will not sanctify the lie.
His works and wonders bear their witness;
His judgments strip the proud disguise.
No throne of men can buy their silence.
No threat can make them change their cry.
And now the question reaches closer
Than the stars or shattered stone:
What will I do with truth before me
When the choice becomes my own?
Will I take the lie that shields me
From the grief of being wrong?
Or embrace the One I have resisted—
YahuShua—all along?
Not the voice that flatters.
Not the hand that buys.
Not the dazzling promise
That demands I close my eyes.
Let my pride be broken.
Let my hiding end.
Truth is not my enemy—
I will turn to Him again.
The first harvest—
His children gathered home.
Let the kingdoms hear the witnesses:
The heavens have a throne!
Glory to the Lord of heaven!
Glory to the righteous King!
His works, His wonders, and His judgments—
Let every nation hear His witnesses sing!
The lie may fill the airwaves;
The truth will not be owned.
YahuShua, our salvation—
To You the glory, Yours alone!
The screens were full of answers.
The streets were full of dust.
I could not choose for all the world—
But I could choose whom I would trust.
